Now produce final answer.<|end_think|>The parity of the sum of a subset depends only on the number of odd elements it contains, because each odd contributes \(1\pmod 2\) and each even contributes \(0\pmod 2\).

*In \(S=\{1,2,\dots ,1441\}\):*  

- odd numbers: \(\displaystyle O=\frac{1441+1}{2}=721\)  
- even numbers: \(\displaystyle E=\frac{1441-1}{2}=720\)

For a \(77\)-element subset let \(k\) be the number of odd elements it contains.  
Then the sum is even iff \(k\) is even, and odd iff \(k\) is odd.

Hence  

\[
\begin{aligned}
A&=\#\{\text{subsets of size }77\text{ with even sum}\}
   =\sum_{\substack{k=0\\k\text{ even}}}^{77}\binom{721}{k}\binom{720}{77-k},\\[2mm]
B&=\#\{\text{subsets of size }77\text{ with odd sum}\}
   =\sum_{\substack{k=0\\k\text{ odd}}}^{77}\binom{721}{k}\binom{720}{77-k}.
\end{aligned}
\]

The difference \(D=A-B\) is

\[
\begin{aligned}
D &=\sum_{k=0}^{77}(-1)^{k}\binom{721}{k}\binom{720}{77-k}\\
  &= [x^{77}]\bigl((1-x)^{721}(1+x)^{720}\bigr) .
\end{aligned}
\]

Since \(721=720+1\),

\[
(1-x)^{721}(1+x)^{720}
   =(1-x)\,(1-x^{2})^{720}.
\]

Only even powers appear in \((1-x^{2})^{720}\).  
Thus the coefficient of \(x^{77}\) comes solely from the term \(-x(1-x^{2})^{720}\):

\[
D= -[x^{76}]\,(1-x^{2})^{720}
   = -\binom{720}{38}(-1)^{38}
   =-\binom{720}{38}.
\]

Therefore  

\[
A-B = -\binom{720}{38}\;<0 .
\]

So the subsets with an **odd** sum are more numerous; Bushra’s count exceeds Ahmad’s by \(\displaystyle\binom{720}{38}\).
